 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Pittsburgh Steelers have deployed an intriguing offensive look over the past couple of weeks. In Weeks 6 and 7, Pittsburgh has increasingly found ways to get both of its running backs involved. While much of that production has come through substitutions and personnel changes, the Steelers have also introduced a wrinkle we haven't seen much of: deploying Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle on the field at the same time .
 To some people's surprise, the approach has been highly effective. Pittsburgh got 127 yards from scrimmage from the duo in Week 6, followed by 223 yards in Week 7. With the Steelers' receiving corps thinned out by injuries, this wrinkle has provided a welcome alternative that has produced results. In Week 8, it could become a difference-making approach that creates a matchup advantage against Cleveland .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Steelers' Efficient Two-Back Usage Could Force Changes From Cleveland's Defense
 Oct 25, 2026; Paris, FRA; New Orleans Saints safety Justin Reid (21) makes a tackle on Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren (30) during the second quarter at Stade de France.Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
 The Steelers rank just 13th in the NFL in two-back personnel usage, with 27 total snaps in the formation. However, they lead the league with a +0.23 EPA per play in that personnel grouping . Through two weeks, Warren and Dowdle have combined for 350 yards from scrimmage, creating a difficult matchup for opposing defenses. Cleveland could be forced to pick its poison in Week 8.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Looking at the Browns' defensive tendencies, Cleveland uses its heaviest non-base personnel package at the highest rate in the NFL (94%) . However, the Browns stack the box just 25.9% of the time, ranking 14th in the league. To their credit, Cleveland's defense has remained highly productive despite trading away its star EDGE rusher this offseason. However, one area where the Browns have struggled with consistency is defending the ground game.
 Steelers' Run Game Could Push Cleveland to Its Limits
 Oct 25, 2026; Paris, FRA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) hands off to running back Jaylen Warren (30) against the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter at Stade de France Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
 Given Cleveland's relatively low rate of heavy-box usage, its struggles against the run aren't particularly surprising. The Browns currently rank 20th in the NFL, allowing 116.4 rushing yards per game. The advanced metrics paint a similar picture. Cleveland ranks 13th in defensive rush EPA (-0.106) and 21st in defensive rush success rate (41.4%) .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement When the Steelers faced Cleveland in Week 4, they found some early success on the ground. Warren rushed for 92 yards, but several offensive mistakes put Pittsburgh behind and forced the offense to rely more heavily on the passing game to play catch-up. In that matchup, the Browns posted a 0.022 defensive rush EPA, ranking 23rd, and a 50.0% defensive rush success rate, ranking 27th.
 It's also worth remembering that the Steelers hadn't introduced their two-back package when these teams met in Week 4. Since then, Pittsburgh has added another dimension to its offense, with both Warren and Dowdle proving effective when deployed together.
 The Browns already have a relatively vulnerable run defense, and Pittsburgh now has another way to challenge its personnel and defensive tendencies. If the Steelers can consistently get both running backs involved, they could create a significant advantage in Week 8. Can Pittsburgh take advantage of the potential mismatch?
